title: ACEF Taxonomy Crosswalk (closed, version-pinned, per-member derived projections of harm_core)
description: The taxonomy_crosswalk object referenced by incident_card (RFC-0002 §5.5, Appendix E Q15; ACEF core_version 1.1.0). Maps one incident to each framework. Every member is OPTIONAL, CLOSED (its own additionalProperties: false), and VERSION-PINNED, and is a DERIVED PROJECTION of harm_core (§5.2): when present a member MUST be consistent with the core, checked by the ACEF-owned one-directional core->scheme derivation rows in harm-core-taxonomy.json (a contradiction raises ACEF-085, §7 — a VALIDATOR-enforced cross-record check, not encoded structurally here). The crosswalk object itself is closed: unknown members are rejected unless `x-*`-namespaced (matching `^x-[a-z0-9-]+(/[a-z0-9-]+)*$`, accepting the bare `x-<vendor>` and the slash-qualified `x-<vendor>/<segment>(/<segment>)*` forms), per the §5.5 / Appendix-E-Q15 closure rule and the repo X6 vendor-namespace pattern (v1.1/manifest.schema.json:96-102). Closure lets the validator catch a misspelled member, a wrong-typed value, or a missing mandatory member — impossible under the Revision 0 additionalProperties: true. Version-pin field: every member uses `edition` EXCEPT `mit_domain`, which uses MIT's own `taxonomy_version` label as its edition pin (no member uses `scheme_version`). Each member's `edition`/`taxonomy_version` is REQUIRED so a populated member is verifiable evidence (schemes drift: NIST draft<->final, CSET v1<->planned, MIT 2024<->2025 subdomains). Determinism: every order-insensitive array (oecd.criteria[], eu_ai_act.serious_incident_triggers[], nist_ai_600_1.categories[], aiid.report_ids[] numeric ascending, stix.object_refs[]) MUST be sorted ascending by the RFC-8785 canonical byte sequence of its elements before hashing and serialization (§5.10). NOTE: members whose CLOSED external value enumeration is not yet transcribed from its primary source (oecd criteria values, cset axes, mit_domain subdomains) validate STRUCTURALLY here (key presence + edition pin + base type) but their value-sets are promoted only on the v1.2 closed-enum conformance surface (§10); nist_ai_600_1.categories is the one external enum already transcribed/verified (§5.5) and is closed here.

^x-[a-z0-9-]+(/[a-z0-9-]+)*(?![\\s\\S]).description: X6 vendor-extension namespace (§5.5 / Appendix E Q15). Accepts both the bare `x-<vendor>` form and the slash-qualified namespace form `x-<vendor>/<segment>(/<segment>)*` documented in the repo (e.g. x-freddy and x-freddy/voice-rubric-emission, as cited in v1.1/manifest.schema.json:95 and present in tests/conformance/golden-bundles/). Segments are lowercase [a-z0-9-]; uppercase keys, non-`x-` keys, and a bare trailing slash (x-freddy/) are rejected. Any matching `x-*` key is accepted, safely-ignorable, preserved on round-trip, and MUST NOT affect conformance; non-`x-` unknown members are rejected by additionalProperties: false.

oecd.description: OECD common reporting framework crosswalk (§5.5). OECD is the canonical anchor; criterion ids key to the OECD ordinal positions (`oecd-crf-2025/<n>`), transcribed from the OECD primary source — not invented. The closed value sets for criteria #3/#19 remain on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10); here the member validates structurally (edition pin + criterion id/value shape).

edition.description: Version-pin (§5.5). The OECD common reporting framework edition (OECD AI Papers No. 34, Feb 2025).

criteria.description: OECD criteria entries; order-insensitive, sorted per §5.10. Each id keys to the OECD ordinal `oecd-crf-2025/<n>`.

id.description: OECD criterion id keyed to the ordinal position (`oecd-crf-2025/<n>`).

value.description: Transcribed criterion value. The closed value enumeration for criteria #3/#19 is on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10); not constrained here.

eu_ai_act.description: EU AI Act Art. 3(49) serious-incident trigger crosswalk (§5.5). The trigger is an ARRAY plus a `widespread` modifier, not a single enum (one incident can satisfy multiple triggers). `death_involved` is carried because 3(49)(a) covers death OR serious health harm; the 10-day clock keys on death only (§5.7).

serious_incident_triggers.description: Art. 3(49)(a-d) trigger letters; order-insensitive, sorted per §5.10. These `3.49.*` TRIGGER codes are crosswalk values, NOT harm_class names (§5.2). The triggers are a SET (uniqueItems: true) — a duplicate ['3.49.a','3.49.a'] is rejected — matching the source-backed twin (card_source.eu_ai_act_facts.serious_incident_triggers) and the §5.5 set semantics; §5.7 reads this same array from the public card to compute the ACEF-084 shortest-applicable clock, so a sorted-set-with-duplicate would be self-contradictory. minItems stays optional here because the whole eu_ai_act member is profile-conditional.

widespread.description: The "widespread infringement" modifier of (c) — a cross-cutting modifier, not a fifth trigger letter (§5.5). Drives the 2-day clock with 3.49.b (§5.7).

death_involved.description: Whether death is involved. NOT derivable from harm_class (3(49)(a) covers death AND non-fatal serious health harm); keys the 10-day clock (§5.7).

cset.description: CSET (csetv1) crosswalk (§5.5). tangibility and the distribution axis live in harm_core, NOT here (Revision 0 duplication removed). The closed value enumerations for the CSET axes remain on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10); here the member validates structurally (edition pin + base types).

harm_type.description: CSET harm type axis. Closed value set on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10).

autonomy.description: CSET autonomy axis (operationalized in the AIID CSETv1 taxonomy). Closed value set on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10).

sector.description: CSET sector axis. Closed value set on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10).

nist_ai_600_1.description: NIST AI 600-1 (July 2024 FINAL) risk-category enrichment (§5.5). A risk-category enrichment, NOT an incident class. The category names are a CLOSED enum verified against the NIST.AI.600-1 final PDF (distinct from the April-2024 draft names); this is the one external enum already transcribed/verified, so it is closed here.

categories.description: NIST AI 600-1 final category names; order-insensitive, sorted per §5.10. Closed enum (verified, §5.5).

mit_causal.description: MIT AI Risk Repository Causal Taxonomy crosswalk (§5.5). entity x intent x timing, mirroring harm_core.causality.

mit_domain.description: MIT AI Risk Repository Domain Taxonomy crosswalk (§5.5). This is the ONLY member that uses MIT's own `taxonomy_version` label as its edition pin (no member uses `scheme_version`). The subdomain closed value sets drift (2024<->2025) and remain on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10); here the member validates structurally (taxonomy_version pin + base types).

taxonomy_version.description: MIT's own taxonomy_version label, used as this member's edition pin (§5.5).

domain.description: MIT domain. Closed value set on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10).

subdomain.description: MIT subdomain (drifts 2024<->2025). Closed value set on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§10).

aiid.description: AI Incident Database soft cross-reference (§5.5). NON-AUTHORITATIVE; hard-links when present but never replaces the incident_dedupe_key spine. AIID's one-incident-to-many-reports model is handled in Appendix E Q6/Q28.

incident_id.description: AIID incident id (integer per Appendix A). Non-authoritative; an upstream AIID renumber MUST NOT invalidate the dedupe key (§5.5).

report_ids.description: AIID report ids; order-insensitive, sorted numeric ascending per §5.10.

stix.description: STIX 2.1 emit-only cross-reference (§5.5, §5.8). object_refs[] MUST be resolvable STIX 2.1 ids (`<type>--<uuidv4>`) pointing to producer-asserted STIX SDOs. Ingest/round-trip is deferred (Appendix E Q27).

object_refs.description: Resolvable STIX 2.1 ids `<type>--<uuidv4>`; order-insensitive, sorted per §5.10. A SET (uniqueItems): duplicates are forbidden, matching the SDK's de-duplicating emission and the sibling serious_incident_triggers[]/harm_distribution_basis[] set arrays.

items.description: A STIX 2.1 id of the form `<type>--<uuidv4>` (RFC 4122 v4 UUID; STIX SDO type token).
